before.en: After Napoleon's first defeat, European powers met in Vienna to negotiate a political settlement. The Final Act reorganized territories and recognized arrangements including the German Confederation; questions concerning Poland and Saxony exposed competing dynastic and strategic interests. The agreement was signed before the Battle of Waterloo, so the settlement cannot simply be described as a reaction to that battle. Vienna shows how treaties combine legal claims, military leverage and compromise. Its boundaries need to be read alongside the interests of people living in the territories assigned by diplomats.
before.zh: 拿破仑首次战败后，欧洲列强在维也纳会商政治安排。《最后议定书》重新划分领土，并确认德意志邦联等制度；波兰与萨克森问题凸显不同王朝和战略利益的竞争。议定书在滑铁卢战役之前已经签署，因此不能简单说成是该战役的结果。维也纳会议显示条约如何结合法律主张、军事力量与妥协；阅读外交官划定的边界时，还应考虑被划入这些领土的人们。

after.en:
After Napoleon's first defeat, European powers met in Vienna to negotiate a political settlement. The Final Act reorganized territories and recognized arrangements including the German Confederation; questions concerning Poland and Saxony exposed competing dynastic and strategic interests. The agreement was signed before the Battle of Waterloo, so the settlement cannot simply be described as a reaction to that battle. Vienna shows how treaties combine legal claims, military leverage and compromise. Its boundaries need to be read alongside the interests of people living in the territories assigned by diplomats.

An 1819 engraving by Jean Godefroy after Jean-Baptiste Isabey assembled the congress into a group portrait. Men gather around a table within a border of portraits and emblems. The composition makes the diplomats visible while also showing how an image produced after negotiations could organize their public memory.

让·戈德弗鲁瓦据伊萨贝原作制作的1819年铜版画，将会议组织为群像：男子聚于桌边，肖像与纹章构成边框。这种构图让外交官变得可见，也展示谈判结束后的图像如何组织公众记忆。

before.en:
The revolutionary upheavals of 1848 opened space for a German national assembly in Frankfurt. Representatives debated political rights, the shape of a proposed state and the relationship between a legislature and a monarch. Political clubs within the assembly expressed competing liberal, democratic and conservative programs rather than one agreed national will.

The project also exposed limits of representation: elections centered on adult independent men, with different procedures in different states. The assembly adopted fundamental rights and a constitution, but the Prussian king refused the imperial crown offered to him in 1849. Reviving monarchical power and military force defeated the constitutional project. Its failure was not an absence of political experimentation. Documents and debates allow comparison with later unification and constitutions, showing that national institutions could be proposed, contested and suppressed before a state possessing them actually existed.
before.zh:
1848年的革命动荡，为法兰克福德国国民议会的召开打开空间。代表们讨论政治权利、拟议国家的形式，以及立法机关与君主的关系。议会内不同政治社团表达自由派、民主派和保守派的竞争方案，并非同一种已经形成的民族意志。

这一项目也显露代表制度的局限：选举围绕具有独立身份的成年男性展开，各邦程序不同。议会通过基本权利与宪法，但普鲁士国王在1849年拒绝所授帝冠。恢复力量的君主政府与军事行动，击败了宪制项目。失败不等于没有政治实验。文书与辩论可与后来的统一和宪法比较，说明在真正具备这些制度的国家出现之前，国家制度已可能被提出、争论并遭压制。

before.en: Shah Abbas I moved the Safavid capital to Isfahan in 1597–1598 and reshaped the city through a new ceremonial square, connected bazaars and major buildings. Royal audience space, mosques and the entrance to the commercial district placed several institutions of government and urban life around one public setting. Court sponsorship also supported painting, manuscripts and decorative arts. The design made connections between commerce and royal authority visible, while the older city remained part of the larger urban system. Construction continued beyond Abbas’s reign, so the square’s surviving ensemble should be read as a developing project rather than a single finished moment.
before.zh: 阿拔斯一世于1597—1598年将萨法维都城迁至伊斯法罕，并通过新礼仪广场、相连的集市及大型建筑重塑城市。王室觐见空间、清真寺和商业区入口，把政府与城市生活的多种机构汇聚在同一公共环境中。宫廷也赞助绘画、手稿和装饰艺术。规划使商业与王权之间的联系可见，而旧城仍属于更大的城市体系。工程在阿拔斯统治结束后继续，因此现存广场建筑群应被视为逐步发展的项目，而非一个瞬间完成的整体。

after.en:
Shah Abbas I moved the Safavid capital to Isfahan in 1597–1598 and reshaped the city through a new ceremonial square, connected bazaars and major buildings. Royal audience space, mosques and the entrance to the commercial district placed several institutions of government and urban life around one public setting. Court sponsorship also supported painting, manuscripts and decorative arts. The design made connections between commerce and royal authority visible, while the older city remained part of the larger urban system. Construction continued beyond Abbas’s reign, so the square’s surviving ensemble should be read as a developing project rather than a single finished moment.

Luigi Pesce photographed the square in 1858 using a paper negative. The surviving salted-paper print sets the open space against arcades, entrances, a dome and minarets. Its much later date separates the Safavid building project from the nineteenth-century city that photography could record.
after.zh:
阿拔斯一世于1597—1598年将萨法维都城迁至伊斯法罕，并通过新礼仪广场、相连的集市及大型建筑重塑城市。王室觐见空间、清真寺和商业区入口，把政府与城市生活的多种机构汇聚在同一公共环境中。宫廷也赞助绘画、手稿和装饰艺术。规划使商业与王权之间的联系可见，而旧城仍属于更大的城市体系。工程在阿拔斯统治结束后继续，因此现存广场建筑群应被视为逐步发展的项目，而非一个瞬间完成的整体。

路易吉·佩谢于1858年以纸负片拍摄广场。存世盐纸照片将开放空间与连拱、入口、圆顶和宣礼塔并置。拍摄年代远晚于萨法维建设工程，因而呈现的是摄影所能记录的十九世纪城市。

before.en:
Greek works reached Arabic readers through several routes, often involving Syriac versions, revisions and the labor of more than one translator. Scholars selected, compared and adapted texts for new audiences. The resulting movement depended on patrons and scholarly communities whose religious affiliations and languages were varied, rather than a single homogeneous group preserving a fixed body of knowledge.

Attributions can be uncertain: a work credited to one translator may survive only in another person’s revision, or be known through a bibliographic notice after the text itself has been lost. Such distinctions matter for understanding intellectual change. This entry therefore describes a network of activity and avoids treating every translation as a product of one institution called the House of Wisdom. Translation made new arguments possible; it was not merely the physical transportation of books.
before.zh:
希腊著作通过多种途径到达阿拉伯语读者，常涉及叙利亚语版本、修订及不止一位译者的劳动。学者选择、比较和调整文本，以面对新读者。这一运动依赖宗教归属和语言各异的资助者与学术社群，而非一个同质群体保存固定知识。

译者归属有时不确定：署于一人名下的作品，可能只留下他人修订本，或原文已失、仅见书目记载。这些区别关系到如何理解思想变化。本条因此描述活动网络，不把每次翻译都归于一所名叫“智慧宫”的机构。翻译使新论证成为可能，不只是书籍的实物搬运。

after.en:
Greek works reached Arabic readers through several routes, often involving Syriac versions, revisions and the labor of more than one translator. Scholars selected, compared and adapted texts for new audiences. The resulting movement depended on patrons and scholarly communities whose religious affiliations and languages were varied, rather than a single homogeneous group preserving a fixed body of knowledge.

Attributions can be uncertain: a work credited to one translator may survive only in another person’s revision, or be known through a bibliographic notice after the text itself has been lost. Such distinctions matter for understanding intellectual change. This entry therefore describes a network of activity and avoids treating every translation as a product of one institution called the House of Wisdom. A 1224 illustrated Arabic manuscript of Dioscorides gives a later material witness to this transmission. In a scene attributed to Baghdad, figures prepare a honey-based medicine beneath a shelf of vessels. Copying, painting and reading kept translated knowledge in use long after the initial translation; this page is not an original translator’s manuscript.
